copy.meter_near: {n} / {hard} memories — close to the tested limit
copy.meter_beyond: {n} / {hard} memories — beyond the tested range: answers are unreliable
copy.capacity_note: This stores your first ~1,000 memories reliably-ish. Beyond that it is unreliable — this is a known limitation of the project as of now.

capabilities.example: Claude wrote TTL = 60 min on Monday, Codex wrote 30 min on Wednesday → you see only 30 min; the timeline lists both writes.
Two agents word the same fact differently → it may show BOTH as current until you confirm.
An external web page tries to overwrite a human decision → quarantined, shown only as UNTRUSTED.
Claude's private note is never shown to Codex or the voice agent.
Claude and Codex write different values at the same moment → it should show a conflict, but sometimes shows one value as current.
Undo everything after Tuesday 10:00 → the brain answers exactly as it did then.
"What's the TTL?" when there are three TTLs → you may get only some of them.

known_flaws.text: Reworded updates can leave the old value marked current.
Above 1,000 memories it finds the current value much less often.
Automatic self-heal hid correct memories in tests, so it needs your approval.
The experimental same-fact detector did not reduce stale values in tests and is OFF.
